To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the use of polypropylene felt (PPF) and nylon media for anaerobic suspended particle attached growth fermentation of screened swine wastewater was feasible and the combination of both materials provided the highest methane yield.

1) both media were suitable for use in a SPAG fermenter; 2) the polypropylene felt media performed best at a 7.5 FR and the nylon media performed best at 15 FR; 3) the polypropelene felt media was more stable and less prone to clogging than the nylon; and 4) a combination of the media would be the best choice to maximize performance.
the 7.5 % fill ratio was the optimum fill ratio for both the polypropylene and the reticulated nylon media.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a process that can be used to convert swine waste to a methane-rich biogas.

the following: 1) the development of an anaerobic process for the treatment of screened flushed swine waste, 2) the development of a process for the production of methane from screened flushed swine wastes, 3) the development of process for the recovery of methane from anaerobic digestion systems, and 4) the development of anaerobic digestion technology for use in swine production systems.
the development of a SPAG process that is capable of treating a variety of waste streams, including those with low organic loading concentrations.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
both media are equally suitable for use as a SPAG media.
the 15% FR of the 100 micron felt and 15% FR reticulated nylon media were the most suitable for use in the SPAG fermenters.
the reticulated nylon media is the most desirable of the two media tested.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
SPAG fermentation can be used to produce methane gas from flushed swine waste liquid.

the SPAG process can be used to treat screened flushed swine waste with high levels of suspended solids and volatile solids, but that the media used to support the attached growth is a critical factor in process performance.
SPAG fermentation is a promising technology for the treatment of swine waste liquids and that further work is needed to optimize the process.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the 15% media fill ratio is superior to 7.5%.
a media fill ratio of 7.50% is adequate for the 25L reactors tested.
a combination of 15% FR polypropylene felt with 7.5 % FR reticulated nylon media is the most suitable media combination for SPAG fermentation.
